title: IMVT Investment Memo
recommendation: Cautious; lead-asset rNPV covers only ~5% of market cap, priced for more than MG alone.
thesis: rNPV of $0.4B (pos 0.38, unadjusted NPV $1.0B) versus an $8.11B market cap means MG alone explains under 5% of value. The market is pricing in either a much larger multi-indication franchise (RA, SjD, CIDP, GD, CLE) or a materially higher PoS than our 38% MG-only estimate. Cash of $797.8M funds the program through key 2026-2028 readouts, but no BLA has been filed and prior-generation batoclimab failed two Phase 3 TED trials, tempering confidence in near-term execution.
variant_view: At $39.25/share and $8.11B market cap, the price implies the market is valuing IMVT well beyond the lead MG asset's rNPV coverage (~5% of cap), effectively pricing in success and revenue contribution across multiple pipeline indications (RA, SjD, CIDP, GD, CLE) simultaneously, not just MG. Our evidence supports only the MG asset at a 0.38 probability of success [peak_sales], derived from a company-disclosed addressable population of 27,500 patients versus a 56,000-patient epidemiology base [9][10] - a single-indication read, not a franchise one. The gap is large: if the market's multi-indication assumption is wrong and only MG succeeds, fair value implied by rNPV is roughly $0.4B versus the ~$8B priced in, a >90% disconnect. This is resolvable by the GD Phase 3 top-line readout expected in 2027 [regulatory] and earlier signal from the D2T RA open-label cohort data [pos]; positive reads across multiple indications would validate the franchise pricing, while a repeat of batoclimab's TED Phase 3 failures [7] would confirm the single-asset, MG-only valuation view.

sections.title: Executive Summary & Thesis
sections.takeaway: Cautious; lead-asset rNPV covers only ~5% of market cap, priced for more than MG alone.

sections.title: Company & Pipeline Overview
sections.takeaway: IMVT's lead asset IMVT-1402, an FcRn inhibitor targeting pathogenic IgG-driven autoimmune disease, posted a 72.7% ACR20 response at Week 16 in a potentially registrational Phase 2/3 D2T RA trial, with a differentiated safety profile versus the company's earlier FcRn candidate batoclimab.
sections.prose: IMVT-1402 inhibits FcRn to lower pathogenic IgG levels, the proposed mechanism across the company's autoimmune pipeline [1][2][3]. In a Phase 2/3 D2T RA trial, ACR20/50/70 response rates at Week 16 were 72.7%/54.5%/35.8% [4][6]. The company's prior FcRn asset, batoclimab, showed a 77% mean IgG reduction and 80% ATD-free response rate at 12 weeks in Graves' disease, with durability to ~80% maintained at Week 48 off-treatment, and deeper IgG reduction correlating with better response (64% vs 23%) [7][8][9][10][11][12][14][15]. Batoclimab caused treatment-related lipid elevations prompting a voluntary dosing pause; IMVT-1402 has not shown this effect [5][17]. Cash position not disclosed in provided claims.

sections.title: Mechanism of Action
sections.takeaway: Mechanism is well-supported by pharmacodynamic and clinical linkage across two molecules: FcRn blockade lowers pathogenic IgG, and deeper IgG reduction tracks with clinical response, with batoclimab's 77% mean IgG reduction pairing with an 80% ATD-free response rate in Graves' disease [6][7][8][9].
sections.prose: IMVT-1402 inhibits FcRn to lower pathogenic IgG in autoimmune disease [3], the same mechanism validated by predecessor batoclimab. In Graves' disease, batoclimab cut mean IgG by 77% at 12 weeks alongside an 80% response rate [6][7][8][9], and responders with ≥70% IgG reduction had a 64% ATD-free response rate versus 23% for lesser reducers [10][11], directly linking IgG lowering to clinical benefit. Response was durable: ~80% maintained thyroid hormone control 24 weeks off-treatment [12][13]. In IMVT-1402's D2T RA trial, ACR20/50/70 rates were 72.7%/54.5%/35.8% at Week 16 [4][5], though this is open-label, single-arm data. Class-level support comes from nipocalimab, where IgG/ACPA reduction correlated with RA response [15] and a placebo-controlled Sjögren's trial hit its primary endpoint [14]. Key differentiator: batoclimab caused lipid elevations prompting a dosing pause [16]; IMVT-1402 has not shown this signal [17].

sections.title: Probability of Success
sections.takeaway: We estimate a 30-45% probability of success for IMVT-1402 across its lead indications, reflecting supportive mechanistic data offset by largely unread pivotal trials and a checkered program history [1]-[14].
sections.prose: IMVT-1402 benefits from regulatory precedent (an anti-FcRn agent is already approved in CIDP) [15] and strong biomarker/efficacy data from predecessor batoclimab in Graves' disease (77% mean IgG reduction, 80% responder rate, ~80% durable off-treatment thyroid normalization at 24 weeks) [16][17][25][26]. Trial designs across Graves', SjD, and CIDP are randomized, placebo-controlled, with clinically meaningful endpoints [19][20][21], and an open-label RA cohort showed a clean safety signal [27]. But this is a wide, uncertain band: no BLA has ever been filed [32], the RA program's controlled endpoint is still pending [23][24], CLE support rests on two patients [18], and four batoclimab trials (TED, GO, CIDP, WAIHA) were terminated [28][29][30][31], with the company itself cautioning biomarker gains may not translate to pivotal efficacy [33].

sections.title: Regulatory Path
sections.takeaway: IMVT-1402 has three potentially registrational programs underway (MG, GD, D2T RA) but no confirmed regulatory designations, no filing timeline beyond GD topline data in CY2027, and an undisclosed accelerated-vs-full approval pathway.
sections.prose:
- IMVT-1402 (MG): Phase 3, potentially registrational trial ongoing; no results timeline disclosed [1][18].
- IMVT-1402 (GD): Second potentially registrational trial with primary endpoint of euthyroid/off ATD at week 26; topline results expected CY2027 [2][17]; endpoint is a clinical outcome measure, more consistent with full approval than a surrogate-based accelerated pathway [12][13].
- IMVT-1402 (D2T RA): Preliminary open-label Phase 3-stage efficacy data reported (Week 16 ACR response rates) from a potentially registrational trial [3].
- Batoclimab: Development discontinued across all indications after two Phase 3 TED trials missed primary endpoint (proptosis responder rate at week 24); orphan drug designation for MG granted by FDA (July 2021) and EC (August 2022) is now moot given discontinuation [4][5][6][7].
- Designations for IMVT-1402: Company may seek orphan drug designation but none granted to date; no fast track, breakthrough therapy, or EMA PRIME designation disclosed [8][9][10][11].
- Open question: whether IMVT-1402 will pursue accelerated or full approval is not disclosed for any indication; any accelerated pathway would require post-marketing confirmatory studies with withdrawal risk if benefit isn't verified [14][15][16][20]; autoinjector presentation would add combination-product review complexity [19].

sections.title: Commercial Opportunity
sections.takeaway: Illustrative gross peak-sales range of $0.5-1.2B for IMVT-1402 in MG, built on assumed penetration/pricing inputs rather than disclosed guidance.
sections.prose: No public epidemiology or pricing exists for this pre-commercial asset, so this range is illustrative, not a forecast. The company discloses ~20,000-35,000 US MG patients inadequately controlled on standard of care; the model uses the midpoint, ~27,500 patients, as the addressable pool [5]. This implies roughly 49% of the estimated ~56,000 total US MG prevalent population (derived from Orphanet's 1-5/10,000 rate) are addressable [1][2][3]. Applying assumed peak penetration and net pricing to the 27,500-patient pool yields gross peak sales of $0.5-1.2B, with a deterministic base case of ~$0.82B gross before risk adjustment [6][7]. A 65% probability of success — assumed from typical late-stage biologic rates for a validated FcRn mechanism, not company-disclosed — is applied separately in valuation, producing a risk-adjusted base near $0.54B [4]. Treat all figures as order-of-magnitude, not point estimates.

sections.title: Valuation & Price vs Thesis
sections.takeaway: Lead-asset rNPV of ~$0.4B covers roughly 5% of IMVT's $8.11B market cap, implying the market is pricing in substantial value beyond the modeled asset — pipeline optionality, platform, or upside cases not captured in this estimate.
sections.prose: At $39.25/share, the market values Immunovant at $8.11B. Our deterministic rNPV for the lead asset alone is ~$0.4B (unadjusted NPV $1.0B probability-weighted at 0.38 POS), an order-of-magnitude figure, not a price target. Read as a coverage ratio, rNPV/market cap is roughly 5% — the gap is the value the market assigns to items outside this single-asset model (pipeline, optionality, platform), not upside to a target. Balance sheet: $797.8M cash as of June 30, 2026 [1][2][3], down from $902.1M at March 31, 2026 [4], against quarterly operating cash burn of $124.4M [26] and FY26 burn of $407.3M [27]. No debt is disclosed in the evidence reviewed [12]. No explicit runway figure is disclosed [28]. The rNPV/market-cap gap, not the cash position, is where our read most departs from what the price implies.

sections.title: Risks
sections.takeaway: Batoclimab's failure across both Phase 3 TED trials removes a full pipeline asset and raises pipeline-concentration risk, while cash burn of $124.4 million in a single quarter [10] narrows the runway cushion despite $797.8 million on hand [1][2][3].
sections.prose:
- Pipeline concentration: batoclimab was discontinued across all indications after both Phase 3 TED studies missed primary endpoint, eliminating a previously separate asset and leaving thesis more dependent on remaining programs [5].
- Cash burn trend: quarterly operating cash outflow of $124.4 million [10] against cash of $797.8 million at June 30, 2026 [1][2][3], down from $902.1 million at March 31, 2026 [6], implies a shrinking buffer if burn persists at this rate.
- Capital structure: 206,264,878 common shares outstanding [4] plus 10,000 Series A preferred held by RSL [7] and authorization for up to 500,000,000 common shares [8] signal capacity for further dilutive issuance.
- Cash trajectory: year-over-year cash rose from $714.0 million (FY2025) [9] to $902.1 million (FY2026) [6] before declining to $797.8 million post-quarter [1][2][3], underscoring reliance on financing events to sustain the balance rather than operating cash generation.

sections.title: Catalysts
sections.takeaway: The claims name no dated upcoming readouts or filings; the only pipeline catalyst on record is the negative one already reported — batoclimab's discontinuation after two Phase 3 TED misses [5].
sections.prose:
- Batoclimab: development discontinued across all indications after both Phase 3 TED studies failed their primary endpoint; no further readouts pending for this asset [5].
- Cash runway: $797.8M cash as of June 30, 2026 [1][2][3], down from $902.1M at March 31, 2026 [6], with $124.4M used in operations in the June quarter [10] — pace of spend is the metric to watch for future financing needs, though no specific financing or funding event is disclosed.
- No other dated catalysts, trial readouts, or regulatory filing decisions are identified in the evidence provided.
